name: Konark Sun Temple
timings: Sunrise to sunset (ASI). Light & sound show: Mar–Nov 7:30 & 8:20 PM; Dec–Feb 6:30 & 7:20 PM.
closures: Open all year (ASI monument). No active worship; it is a protected heritage site.
entry: ASI ticket: Indians & SAARC/BIMSTEC ₹40 cash / ₹35 online; other foreigners ₹600 cash / ₹550 online; under-15 free.

booking.name: ASI online entry ticket (via ASI 'Must See' page)

dress_code: No formal dress code (monument). Modest clothing, a hat and comfortable footwear are advisable.
rules: Do not climb on, touch or deface carvings
Follow ASI barricades and restricted zones
Light & sound show tickets are sold separately at the venue
Keep the UNESCO site litter-free
best_time: October to February (winter); ASI lists winter as the best season.

festivals.name: International Sand Art Festival, Chandrabhaga Beach
Chandrabhaga Mela / Magha Saptami
festivals.when: Magha Shukla Saptami (Jan–Feb); holy dip at Chandrabhaga

reach.road: 35 km NE of Puri via Marine Drive; ~65 km from Bhubaneswar. Regular buses to Konark Bus Station.
reach.local: Walk from Konark bus stand; autos/taxis to Chandrabhaga Beach (~1 km) and Puri.

avg_visit_time: 2–3 hours (plus ~45 min for the evening light & sound show)
tips: Arrive at opening for cooler weather, softer light and fewer crowds
Book online to save ₹5 per ticket and skip the cash queue
Hire an approved guide to understand the wheel sundials and carvings
Combine with Chandrabhaga Beach and Puri on the Marine Drive route
Carry water and sun protection; there is little shade in the complex
notes: Elevation not verified from an authoritative source (coastal, near sea level). A secondary source says the light & sound show is closed on Mondays; not confirmed officially. Show ticket prices are approximate per Odisha Tourism.

name: Somnath Jyotirlinga Temple
timings: Darshan 6:00 AM–10:00 PM. Aarti 7:00 AM, 12:00 noon, 7:00 PM. 'Jay Somnath' light & sound show 8–9 PM.
closures: Open all year. Light & sound show not held in the monsoon/rainy season.
entry: Free entry. Pooja vidhi and guest houses are paid.

booking.name: Shree Somnath Trust – Online Pooja Vidhi / Donation & Guest House booking

dress_code: Indian wear, trousers, T-shirts and skirts allowed; mini skirts and disrespectful dress not permitted.
rules: Mobiles, cameras, smartwatches and all electronics prohibited; free cloak room lockers
Photography strictly prohibited inside
Remove footwear; free shoe house near the cloak room
No smoking anywhere near the temple
Prayer open to persons with faith in Hinduism (per Trust FAQ)
best_time: October to March for pleasant coastal weather; Shravan month and Mahashivratri for festivities (crowded).

reach.road: Well connected by GSRTC buses; Somnath ST bus stand ~0.8 km. Ahmedabad ~400 km, Junagadh ~82 km.
reach.local: Walk or auto-rickshaw. Trust's Tirth Darshan bus to nearby shrines leaves main gate at 8:30 AM & 3:30 PM.

avg_visit_time: 2–3 hours (half day with light & sound show and nearby tirthas)
tips: Deposit phones at the free cloak room before queueing; no electronics are allowed
Stay for the evening aarti and the 8 PM light & sound show (not in monsoon)
Book Trust guest houses (Sagar Darshan, Lilavati, Maheshwari) online in advance
Wheelchairs/golf carts at main gate and a lift inside help seniors
Visit Bhalka Tirth and Triveni Sangam via the Trust's Tirth Darshan bus
notes: Elevation not verified (seashore). Trust FAQ lists Diu (85 km) as nearest airport and Somnath station at 0.5 km; Keshod (57 km) and 2.5 km station distance are from Wikipedia/utsav.gov.in. Sthapana Divas date (11 May) is from general history, not the Trust FAQ.

name: Dwarkadhish Temple (Jagat Mandir)
timings: Darshan 6:30 AM–1:00 PM and 5:00–9:30 PM. Mangla Aarti 6:30 AM, Sandhya Aarti ~7:30 PM, Shayan Aarti ~8:30 PM.
closures: Open all year. Darshan pauses briefly for bhog/rituals; closed ~1–5 PM. Timings change on festival days.
entry: Free general darshan. No official VIP darshan; seva/bhog offerings are paid.

booking.name: Shree Dwarkadhish Temple – Online Bhog/Seva & Donation

dress_code: Clothes suited to Indian culture. Shorts, mini/midi skirts, sleeveless tops, low-waist jeans and short T-shirts are not allowed.
rules: Deposit mobiles, cameras and leather items at lockers before entry
No photography inside the temple
Remove footwear before entering
Short or revealing clothes will be refused entry
Beware of agents selling 'VIP' darshan; general darshan is free
best_time: October to March; Janmashtami for festivities (very crowded).

reach.road: NH-947 links Dwarka with Jamnagar and Porbandar. Dwarka ST bus stand ~1.2 km from temple.
reach.local: Autos and walking around old town; Gomti Ghat via 56 steps from Swarg Dwar. Bet Dwarka via Sudarshan Setu.

tips: Reach before Mangla Aarti (6:30 AM) for shorter queues
Check the ritual break schedule; darshan pauses during bhog
Dip at Gomti Ghat and enter via Swarg Dwar as per tradition
Wear traditional clothes to avoid being turned away
Pair with Rukmini Temple, Nageshwar Jyotirlinga and Bet Dwarka
notes: Detailed aarti slot times come from a secondary source and match the Ministry of Tourism darshan hours; the official site has no published timings page. Jamnagar airport (JGA) is also used. Festival list beyond Janmashtami is general knowledge, not from an official schedule.

name: Kedarnath Temple
timings: Abhishek pujas early morning (book slot at counter a day prior). Evening aarti ~6:00 PM in summer. No fixed public darshan timetable published.
closures: Seasonal: 2026 season opened 22 Apr (8 AM); closes for winter on Bhai Dooj, 11 Nov 2026. Winter puja at Omkareshwar Temple, Ukhimath.
entry: Free darshan. Mandatory free Char Dham registration. Pujas paid via BKTC; helicopter fares extra.

booking.name: Uttarakhand Char Dham Yatra Registration (mandatory, free)

dress_code: No formal code published; modest clothing. Heavy woollens, rain gear and trekking shoes essential.
rules: Char Dham registration mandatory; QR pass checked at Sonprayag and the Dham
Mobile phones banned in temple premises (2026); photos only at a point ~80 m away
No reels, videography or unauthorised drones
Touching idols, scriptures and bells is prohibited
Night driving on hill roads restricted 10 PM–4 AM
Medical certificate advised for pilgrims over 50 or with health conditions
best_time: May–June and September–October; avoid peak monsoon (July–mid Sept) due to landslides.

festivals.name: Kapat opening
festivals.when: Date fixed on Mahashivratri; Vaishakh (2026: 22 April)

reach.road: Road via Rudraprayag–Guptkashi to Sonprayag; private vehicles stop at Sonprayag. Shuttle (₹50) runs 5 km to Gaurikund.
reach.local: From Gaurikund: walk, pony, palki or porter. Helicopters from Guptkashi, Phata and Sirsi helipads.

trek.notes: Steep uphill trek, typically 6–8 hours. BKTC/UK Tourism say 16 km; Rudraprayag district says 17 km.

avg_visit_time: 1 day at the Dham (BKTC); plan 2–3 days from Rishikesh/Guptkashi
tips: Register free on the official portal or the Tourist Care Uttarakhand app; use no agents
Book helicopters only on heliyatra.irctc.co.in; tickets sell out within hours of opening
2026 heli round-trip base fares: Guptkashi ₹12,154, Phata ₹9,680, Sirsi ₹6,086 (plus GST)
Start the trek at dawn and acclimatise; carry woollens, rain gear and medicines
Deposit your phone at the locker near the temple before darshan
notes: Distances to airport/railway are BKTC figures to Kedarnath road head; BKTC elsewhere quotes 235 km (airport) and 243 km (Rishikesh). Elevation: BKTC states 3,581–3,584 m. Detailed daily darshan hours are not officially published.

name: Badrinath Temple
timings: Abhishek 4:30–6:30 AM; darshan ~7 AM–1 PM and ~4–9 PM (approx.). Evening aarti from ~6 PM; Shayan Aarti after queue clears.
closures: Seasonal: 2026 season opened 23 Apr (6:15 AM); closes for winter on 16 Nov 2026 at 9:37 PM. Closed during solar/lunar eclipses.
entry: Free darshan. Mandatory free Char Dham registration. Pujas paid via BKTC.

booking.name: Uttarakhand Char Dham Yatra Registration (mandatory, free)

puja.name: BKTC online puja booking (Indian mobile number required)

dress_code: No formal code published; modest clothing. Warm woollens needed even in summer.
rules: Char Dham registration mandatory; verify at Pandukeshwar/Badrinath checkpoints
Carry valid government photo ID (passport + visa for foreigners) for pujas
Reach 15–30 min early for booked abhishek, path or aarti
Collect a darshan slot token for smoother darshan
No alcohol or tobacco; do not litter
best_time: May–June and September–October; monsoon brings landslide risk on the highway.

festivals.name: Kapat opening
festivals.when: Date fixed on Basant Panchami (2026: 23 April)

festivals.name: Mata Murti Ka Mela
festivals.when: Annual (Bhadrapada, ~Sept) at Mata Murti temple, Mana

reach.road: Motorable via Rishikesh–Rudraprayag–Joshimath highway. Joshimath ~45 km before Badrinath. Night driving restricted.
reach.local: Temple is a short walk from Badrinath town; Mana village 3 km by road; Tapt Kund beside the temple.

avg_visit_time: 1 day (BKTC); stay at Joshimath or Badrinath
tips: Register free on the official portal before travel; skip unofficial sites charging fees
Bathe at Tapt Kund (hot spring) before darshan, as is tradition
Join the queue early morning; afternoons have a ritual break
Visit Mana village, Vyas Gufa and Bheem Pul (~3 km)
Check weather and road status; landslides can close the highway
notes: General darshan hours (7 AM–1 PM, 4–9 PM) are from secondary sources; BKTC publishes only puja/aarti slot times. Elevation 3,133 m per Wikipedia (infobox says 3,100 m). Mata Murti Mela timing is approximate.
